lufthansa flies back to profit german airline lufthansa has returned to profit in 2004 after posting huge losses in 2003. in a preliminary report the airline announced net profits of 400m euros ($527.61m; £274.73m) compared with a loss of 984m euros in 2003. operating profits were at 380m euros ten times more than in 2003. lufthansa was hit in 2003 by tough competition and a dip in demand following the iraq war and the killer sars virus. it was also hit by troubles at its us catering business. last year lufthansa showed signs of recovery even as some european and us airlines were teetering on the brink of bankruptcy. the board of lufthansa has recommended paying a 2004 dividend of 0.30 euros per share. in 2003 shareholders did not get a dividend. the company said that it will give all the details of its 2004 results on 23 march.

lufthansa flies back to profit german airline lufthansa has returned to profit in 2004 after posting huge losses in 2003. in a preliminary report the airline announced net profits of 400m euros ($527.61m; £274.73m) compared with a loss of 984m euros in 2003. operating profits were at 380m euros ten times more than in 2003. lufthansa was hit in 2003 by tough competition and a dip in demand following the iraq war and the killer sars virus. it was also hit by troubles at its us catering business. last year lufthansa showed signs of recovery even as some european and us airlines were teetering on the brink of bankruptcy. the board of lufthansa has recommended paying a 2004 dividend of 0.30 euros per share. in 2003 shareholders did not get a dividend. the company said that it will give all the details of its 2004 results on 23 march.

Examples: "The company plans to expand into emerging markets with high consumer demand, leveraging its innovative product line." | "New regulatory changes have created an opening for the firm to enter the renewable energy sector with minimal barriers."
- neutral: A neutral statement presents factual, routine, or administrative information without implying significant positive or negative impact on the company’s future performance or outlook, including disclosures that are standard or non-material. Examples: "The annual shareholder meeting will be held on June 15 via webcast." | "The company filed its quarterly financial report with the SEC in accordance with standard procedures."
- risk: A risk describes a potential threat or adverse condition that could negatively affect the company’s operations, financial results, or strategic goals, going beyond normal business fluctuations to highlight material vulnerabilities. Examples: "The company faces increasing competition from low-cost providers, which may erode market share and margins." | "Reliance on a single supplier for critical components exposes operations to disruption in the event of supply chain failures."
